text: Grievances must be submitted within 90 days from the date of occurrence. Grievances submitted after 90 days shall not be entertained unless supported by valid documentary evidence.

A grievance submission must include applicant’s full name, registered mobile number and email ID, institution name, detailed description of the grievance, and supporting documents if applicable. Incomplete submissions may be rejected.
Scholarship-related grievances shall be resolved within 30 working days.
A grievance shall be rejected if it falls outside the defined scope, is submitted beyond the 90-day limit without justification, mandatory information is missing, or the matter is sub judice.

Every Higher Education Institution under the Department of Higher Education, Government of West Bengal shall maintain a formal grievance redressal mechanism for students, faculty and staff to address complaints relating to academic administration, examinations, scholarships, infrastructure, and institutional services.

Each institution shall designate a Grievance Redressal Officer responsible for receiving, registering and processing grievances submitted through the official grievance portal or through institutional channels.
Upon receipt of a grievance, the institution shall acknowledge the complaint and assign a unique grievance registration number to enable tracking and follow-up.
Grievances received through the official portal shall be examined by the concerned authority and forwarded to the relevant department or institution for necessary action and resolution.

Institutions shall ensure that grievances relating to administrative delays, examination results, scholarship disbursement, or student services are reviewed promptly and appropriate corrective measures are initiated.

In cases where the grievance concerns examination evaluation, rechecking or result correction, the institution shall follow the applicable examination regulations and communicate the outcome to the applicant.
If a grievance cannot be resolved at the institutional level, it may be escalated to the Department of Higher Education, Government of West Bengal for further review and appropriate direction.
Applicants shall be informed about the progress and final resolution of their grievance through the registered communication channel, including email or mobile notification.
Anonymous complaints or grievances submitted without verifiable contact details may not be processed unless they contain sufficient evidence of serious administrative irregularity.
Grievances that are already pending before a court of law or judicial authority shall not be entertained by the administrative grievance redressal mechanism.
Misuse of the grievance redressal system through repeated or malicious complaints may lead to administrative action and closure of the grievance.
